title: Dystrail Satire Workshop — v3 · Complete First-Pass Rewrite

paragraphs.text: Dystrail satire workshop

Edit the English directly. Each entry gives the situation, a lead-in, and the player’s choices with the response after each choice. Keep the action clear; make the joke about the policy, boast, or bureaucracy. Aim for one or two sentences per lead-in, a short choice, and one sentence per response. Approved copy will go back into the game before translations are updated.
Three to try first
These are proposed alternatives. Keep the lead-in you like, or replace it. The other tabs contain current English starters for the rest of the review.
The Patriotic Parts Counter
Scenario: Trump’s parts tariffs reach a fictional roadside shop. Your crew can buy an emergency kit, question the invoice, or leave.
Choose or rewrite the lead-in
The mechanic says China is paying Trump’s tariff. China appears to be the name of your debit card.
The roadside kit comes with a patriotic surcharge. Apparently freedom isn’t free, and neither is the sticker.
The shop has two prices: before the tariff announcement and after the tariff announcement. Both are your problem.
Choices → responses
Buy the roadside kit. → You get the supplies. China still hasn’t offered to split the bill.
Ask the mechanic to explain the invoice. → Parts, tariff, markup, freedom handling fee. Freedom is the only item with no return policy.
Keep moving. → You leave before the clerk tariffs the conversation.
The Eight-Billion-Dollar Pothole
Scenario: A fictional DOGE-style board overstates savings while a pothole stays unfixed. The real hook is one contract entry corrected from $8 billion to $8 million.
Choose or rewrite the lead-in
The DOGE-style board claims eight billion in savings. Someone checks the zeroes. The pothole asks whether anyone has checked for a shovel.
The savings board has lost three zeroes. The pothole has lost no depth.
The board declares the pothole eliminated. Your suspension has filed a dissenting opinion.
Choices → responses
Count the zeroes on camera. → The savings shrink. The hole retains its original dimensions.
Take the paid patching shift. → You fix the road. The efficiency dashboard takes the credit.
Keep moving. → The pothole remains the most transparent part of the budget.
Cabinet Chat: Guest Access
Scenario: A fictional checkpoint chat has unknown guests. The hook is the Trump administration’s Signal chat accidentally including a journalist during military-operation discussions.
Choose or rewrite the lead-in
The checkpoint has adopted the administration’s Signal protocol: a secure chat, total confidence, and someone asking whether this is the book club.
“End-to-end encrypted,” says the checkpoint officer. “We just haven’t checked who’s at either end.”
The briefing is classified. The invite link is on the lunch menu.
Choices → responses
Check everyone’s name before sharing the route. → The dentist’s patient leaves. National security improves without a software update.
Post the itinerary and a thumbs-up. → External Guest 4 reacts with a heart. Intelligence has never been so affirming.
Keep moving. → You leave the chat before being promoted to Secretary of Lunch.
Money and paperwork
Rewrite the lead-ins, choices, and responses below. These are current English starters; preserve what each choice does. Before the arrow is the button; after it is the response.
Tariffs
The joke: a patriotic promise reaches an ordinary customer as a bigger bill. Background
Service Station Handoff
Scenario: A union shop offers vehicle checks while parts prices are rising; get a tune-up, teach apprentices, or replace the wipers.
Lead-in
A union shop offers uptime checks before you push east.
Choices → responses
Tune up everything → They torque every bolt for the road ahead.
Spot train their apprentices → Skill shares buy future roadside favors.
Swap for better wipers → Rain bands seem less ominous now.
Union Solidarity Blockade
Scenario: Union members affected by tariff uncertainty offer a protective slowdown; coordinate it, pass quietly, or provide snacks.
Lead-in
A local union offers to stage a slowdown so you can pass unharassed.
Choices → responses
Coordinate the action → Their action buys you a clear lane and louder endorsements.
Slip through quietly → You stay discreet but the blockade still slows pursuers.
Coordinate relief snacks → Union stewards cheer the solidarity.
Circuit Breaker Audit
Scenario: Engineers find the convoy’s power system overloaded while replacement parts are costly; stop for repairs, patch it, or buy batteries.
Lead-in
Engineers beg to inspect the convoy's overloaded power grid.
Choices → responses
Authorize downtime → The rolling office powers up safer than before.
Patch and roll → Quick fixes hum but risk a later blowout.
Commission mobile batteries → Reserve packs stabilize the briefing room feed.
Tariff Whiplash
Scenario: A clerk presents a fresh tariff bill for supplies; pay, smuggle the goods, or seek a waiver.
Lead-in
Your previous emergency has been ruled invalid. Please pay for the replacement emergency. The clerk has a fresh tariff stamp and absolutely no refund cash.
Choices → responses
Pay the tariff → You absorb the hit and keep the paperwork tidy.
Smuggle it → Border Beagle sniffs judgement.
Lobby for a waiver → A late-night call buys leniency on the manifest.
Rust Belt Convoy
Scenario: Freight drivers dealing with tariff disruption offer an escort past barricades; follow the lead truck or stay in the middle.
Lead-in
Freight drivers offer to pace you past barricades.
Choices → responses
Draft with the lead truck → You hitch into the convoy and chew up miles.
Hold the middle lane → [Write a short response.]
The Tariff Relabeling Shift
Scenario: A freight yard keeps relabeling shipments as tariff rules change; take a paid shift, trade paperwork help for supplies, or leave.
Lead-in
A freight yard responding to Trump’s tariffs needs help moving boxes between CURRENT RATE and PLEASE CHECK AGAIN. The labels are wearing out first.
Choices → responses
Take a paid loading shift → You earn actual dollars moving hypothetical certainty.
Trade paperwork help for supplies → The dispatcher pays in snacks with a stable exchange rate.
Keep moving → You keep your resources and leave the opportunity behind.
DOGE accounting
The joke: celebrate impressive savings before checking the arithmetic. The historical hook is a specific $8 billion entry corrected to $8 million. Background
Memorandum Dump
Scenario: A pile of sealed memos needs scrutiny after a much-publicized DOGE accounting error; prioritize, pass to oversight, or archive it.
Lead-in
Compressed drives of sealed memos await triage.
Choices → responses
Sort by threat level → You surface red-flags before the opposition.
Forward to oversight → The committee braces for impact early.
Archive for later → You buy a breather but risk surprise later.
Watchdog Sync
Scenario: Inspectors compare reports after DOGE’s billion-to-million correction; contribute evidence, listen, or leak a summary.
Lead-in
Inspectors general huddle to compare sealed reports.
Choices → responses
Share your dossiers → Cross-agency leads seal future subpoenas.
Listen quietly → You bank intelligence without stirring waters.
Leak summary notes → Anonymous memos raise scrutiny everywhere.
Beltway Fast Pass
Scenario: Policy aides who insist on accountable government offer you privileged access through traffic; take the shoulder or ease through the lane.
Lead-in
Policy aides flash badges to keep traffic enforcement off you.
Choices → responses
Ride the cleared shoulder → Security waves you down the empty lane.
Split the lane politely → [Write a short response.]
The Museum of Very Large Savings
Scenario: A museum exaggerates donation totals while commemorating DOGE’s accounting error; audit it for pay, applaud the numbers, or leave.
Lead-in
The exhibit commemorating DOGE’s billion-to-million correction has a donation box labeled TRILLIONS. The curator needs someone who understands decimal places.
Choices → responses
Audit the exhibit for an honorarium → The museum pays thirteen dollars. You verify all thirteen.
Applaud the trillion-dollar quarter → The applause is tremendous. The accounting is performance art.
Keep moving → You keep your resources and leave the opportunity behind.
Five accomplishments
The joke: proving useful work took place becomes more work than doing it. The hook is the administration’s demand for five weekly accomplishments. Background
The Efficiency Emergency
Scenario: An efficiency drive dismissed a bridge crew that has returned to help anyway; contribute parts or document the unfinished work.
Lead-in
An efficiency drive dismissed the bridge crew. The crew came back to help anyway; the savings board still celebrates their eliminated salaries. Lend a hand or document what the board leaves out.
Choices → responses
Donate spare parts to speed the work → The crew waves you onto the priority lane.
Document the backlog for the hotline → Your report pressures the agency to staff up.
Mail Drop Pickup
Scenario: Supporters deliver letters asking what you have accomplished; read them, record a reply, or sort urgent requests.
Lead-in
Supporters sprint over with a bundle of letters asking for updates.
Choices → responses
Read every letter → You share the letters over dinner and spirits lift.
Record a thank-you video → The volunteers upload your message across the network.
Pre-sort the pile → You surface the urgent letters and build goodwill.
Deep State Dirge
Scenario: A hearing about accountability drags on; keep pushing, leave, or call a recess.
Lead-in
A shadowy hearing drags on for hours.
Choices → responses
Hold the line → You squeeze concessions into the transcript.
Cut and run → You duck the cameras and regroup at HQ.
Call a hallway recess → You secure a breather and temper the theatrics.
Overnight Briefing
Scenario: Your exhausted team still faces another accountability briefing; work all night, rotate guards, or call in relief.
Lead-in
Allies urge you to pause, sleep, and align strategy before dawn.
Choices → responses
Power through the night → Another all-nighter leaves everyone frayed.
Set guard rotations → Fresh coffee and shifts let the core team sleep.
Call in the deep bench → Trusted stand-ins hold the line while you recover.
Five Things Corn Did Last Week
Scenario: A farm applies the five-accomplishment email demand to its corn; defend the crop, help with paperwork for pay, or leave.
Lead-in
A farm office has adopted the administration’s five-bullet emails. The corn has submitted four. Management suspects loafing.
Choices → responses
Document the fifth accomplishment: growing → The crop keeps its job. You need a quiet minute.
Help the farmer file for a small fee → Your invoice contains five bullet points. All five say paid.
Keep moving → You keep your resources and leave the opportunity behind.
Please Account for the Bridge
Scenario: Bridge workers must describe their work in five accomplishment bullets; translate the work into paperwork, bring lunch, or leave.
Lead-in
A bridge crew must list five accomplishments in the style of the administration’s emails. Preventing collapse apparently counts as only one.
Choices → responses
Translate structural engineering into five bullets → The bridge is still standing. The email is finally long enough.
Bring lunch while they finish the report → The crew can eat without documenting each bite.
Keep moving → You keep your resources and leave the opportunity behind.
Renaming things
The joke: a grand new name is offered as a substitute for fixing the thing. The hook is Trump’s federal geographic renaming order. Background
Department of Renaming Things
Scenario: Your travel permit no longer matches the renamed destination; decide how to untangle the amendments.
Lead-in
Your permit names yesterday’s destination. Today’s amendments rename it again. The bridge remains structurally unsound, but its name has never been stronger.
Choices → responses
Read every line → You flag riders before they hit the floor.
Skim the highlights → Optimism buys you a short night and long edits later.
Delegate to staff counsel → Your legal lead triages the stack overnight.
Freeway Mural Crew
Scenario: Artists are painting a solidarity mural during a wave of official renaming; join in, fund supplies, or pose for the reveal.
Lead-in
Artists pause your motorcade to finish a solidarity mural.
Choices → responses
Climb a ladder with them → Paint splatters but the livestream loves it.
Fund their paint run → Their co-op texts thanks and fresh designs.
Pose for a quick reveal → The mural trends without blowing schedule.
Neighborhood Watch Brief
Scenario: Block captains are dealing with renamed roads and missing signs; exchange contacts, fix maps, or continue.
Lead-in
Block captains share overnight intel and missing signage.
Choices → responses
Swap hotline contacts → Coordinated texts cover the detour gaps.
Repair their posted maps → The reroute board keeps families moving.
Thank them and roll on → They cheer you through the checkpoint.
Gulf of Parking Lot
Scenario: A rest stop renames a puddle and charges for its new status; paint the sign for pay, fix the route map, or leave.
Lead-in
Following Trump’s renaming spree, a rest stop declares its puddle the Gulf of Premium Parking. The fee applies at low tide too.
Choices → responses
Paint the new sign for seven dollars → A puddle gains prestige. You gain gas money.
Mark the actual exit on the map → The crew escapes without recognizing the puddle’s sovereignty.
Keep moving → You keep your resources and leave the opportunity behind.
The Name Is the Infrastructure
Scenario: An office has given a missing bridge a grand new name; buy a detour permit, demand a usable route, or leave.
Lead-in
The renaming office has learned from Trump’s geographic order. Your missing bridge is now called The Tremendous Connection. The river has not signed off.
Choices → responses
Pay for the newly named detour permit → The permit is excellent. You still take the detour.
Demand a route with physical pavement → The clerk locates a road that exists outside the press release.
Keep moving → You keep your resources and leave the opportunity behind.
Food and services
Rewrite the lead-ins, choices, and responses below. These are current English starters; preserve what each choice does. Before the arrow is the button; after it is the response.
Food support
The joke: a cancellation notice or polished explanation cannot feed anyone. The hook is USDA’s cancellation of the LFPA25 local-food purchasing program. Background
Civic Center Potluck
Scenario: Neighbors hold a potluck after local-food purchasing support was canceled; eat, take meals along, or give back.
Lead-in
Local organizers insist you eat before the next leg.
Choices → responses
Stay for stew → Warm food and stories refill everyone.
Carry meals to go → You promise a shout-out on the livestream.
Donate the stipend back → Their pantry stocks up while the crew beams.
Pop-up Mutual Aid
Scenario: Volunteers replacing canceled food support need supplies and attention; donate, load vans, or broadcast their needs.
Lead-in
Volunteers flag you down to swap supplies for a quick broadcast boost.
Choices → responses
Share supplies and stream their needs → The crew relays your callout down the road.
Help load their vans → A ten minute lift keeps everyone moving.
Set up a rapid signal boost → Your uplink gets their wishlist trending.
Mutual Aid Dispatch Center
Scenario: A mutual-aid dispatch desk is matching food requests to trucks; offer vehicles, improve communications, or learn from them.
Lead-in
Dispatchers dart between radios matching requests to trucks.
Choices → responses
Route your fleet to assist → Dispatchers slot you into priority drop-offs.
Upgrade their signal chain → A clearer net keeps evac traffic flowing.
Observe and take notes → You document best practices for the debrief.
Fundraiser Detour
Scenario: A friendly fundraiser is filling a food-support gap; attend or stay on the route.
Lead-in
You are asked to crash a friendly fundraiser.
Choices → responses
Attend and shake hands → You take home some leftovers.
Skip and stay on route → You gift the organizers an early briefing.
Heartland Waystation
Scenario: Food-aid organizers welcome you onto a cleared stretch of road; exchange favors or stop for coffee.
Lead-in
A local crew waves you onto freshly cleared asphalt.
Choices → responses
Swap favors and push ahead → Local organizers wave you through their shortcut.
Share coffee before rolling out → [Write a short response.]
Locally Grown Funding Gap
Scenario: A co-op has food and hungry neighbors but has lost expected purchasing support; donate supplies, take a paid loading shift, or leave.
Lead-in
After the LFPA25 cancellation, this food co-op has vegetables, hungry neighbors and a federal explanation that contains no recipes.
Choices → responses
Contribute two supply bundles → Dinner survives its encounter with federal priorities.
Take the co-op’s paid loading shift → The co-op pays you. The crates decline to become lighter.
Keep moving → You keep your resources and leave the opportunity behind.
The Shelf Is Still Hungry
Scenario: A co-op needs people to fill the gap left by canceled food purchasing funds; pack food for supplies, do paperwork for pay, or leave.
Lead-in
The LFPA25 cancellation has inspired an agency sign: FOOD ACCESS STREAMLINED. Volunteers are streamlining potatoes into actual bags.
Choices → responses
Help pack food in exchange for three bundles → Your crew gets supplies. Your arms get a government-sized workload.
Handle the co-op’s paid delivery paperwork → The co-op pays ten dollars for forms that finally correspond to food.
Keep moving → You keep your resources and leave the opportunity behind.
Libraries and culture

The joke: public culture has to justify its existence through increasingly absurd paperwork. The hook is the order to reduce the Institute of Museum and Library Services; the scenes are fictional. Background
Crossing Block Party
Scenario: Residents rally for public culture beside a backed-up checkpoint; help with food, take the microphone, or cool the crowd.
Lead-in
Residents host a morale party next to the jammed checkpoint.
Choices → responses
Serve at the grill → Volunteers promise to keep watch overnight.
Headline the mic → Soundbites ripple through the slow-moving line.
Share cooling supplies → Cold towels calm nerves and lower tempers.
Overpass Pop-Up Stage
Scenario: A troupe offers a roadside teach-in about threatened public-culture funding; let them lead or join the panel.
Lead-in
An allied troupe offers to headline a rapid teach-in over the freeway.
Choices → responses
Let them run the program → The troupe's livestream boosts regional momentum.
Join the panel yourself → Your remarks rally the crowd but leave you hoarse.
College Radio Phonebank
Scenario: Students run a radio campaign for public culture; go on air, coach volunteers, or record messages for later.
Lead-in
Students spin up a call-in marathon for signatures.
Choices → responses
Jump on the mic → You juice the call volume with quick riffs.
Train their volunteers → Scripts tighten up and the hotline hums.
Record evergreen promos → Future listeners will still hear your pitch.
The Minimum Viable Library
Scenario: A library prepares an absurdly reduced service after the IMLS reduction order; support readers, digitize its catalog for pay, or leave.
Lead-in
After Trump’s IMLS reduction order, a librarian prepares an emergency plan: one book, chained to a printer that only prints funding applications.
Choices → responses
Supply the volunteer reading table → The children get stories with endings.
Digitize the backup catalog for pay → You preserve the books. The application still wants a fax.
Keep moving → You keep your resources and leave the opportunity behind.
The Exhibit of Pending Funds
Scenario: A museum turns an unresolved grant application into an exhibit; digitize collections for pay, support a tour, or leave.
Lead-in
Following the IMLS reduction order, this museum opens a new exhibit: a velvet rope around the grant application. Nobody may touch its outcome.
Choices → responses
Digitize exhibits for the museum’s day rate → You preserve history before the application becomes an artifact.
Support the volunteer tour → The tour has facts, unlike the funding timetable.
Keep moving → You keep your resources and leave the opportunity behind.
Straws
The joke: a drinking utensil receives the attention normally reserved for a national emergency. The hook is Trump’s paper-straw procurement order. Background
Emergency Straw Reserve
Scenario: A depot prioritizes plastic straws over drinking water; buy water, take a paid inventory shift, or leave.
Lead-in
A roadside depot celebrates Trump’s straw order with a mountain of plastic straws. The water shipment is still pending approval.
Choices → responses
Buy water from the uncelebrated cooler → Water reaches your crew without a signing ceremony.
Inventory the strategic straws for pay → You earn ten dollars and lose the ability to hear the word strategic calmly.
Keep moving → You keep your resources and leave the opportunity behind.
Strategic Straw Inspection
Scenario: A checkpoint turns the paper-straw procurement order into a loyalty test for a cup; offer a drink, read the actual order, or leave.
Lead-in
A checkpoint has interpreted Trump’s paper-straw order as a border doctrine. Your reusable cup is being questioned about its affiliations.
Choices → responses
Offer a sealed drink to end the inspection → The inspector finds the beverage ideologically sufficient.
Read the actual procurement order aloud → The cup is released without charges.
Keep moving → You keep your resources and leave the opportunity behind.
Shower pressure
The joke: ordinary plumbing becomes a presidential achievement. The hook is Trump’s showerhead order. Background
Water Drive Relay
Scenario: A relief post needs drinking water while the political debate is about shower pressure; donate water or help distribute it.
Lead-in
A roadside relief post asks for a quick boost to their hydration drive.
Choices → responses
Donate part of the stash → You refill jugs and leave a short training sheet.
Help with distribution → A coordinated handoff nets you spare filters.
Hydration Sovereignty
Scenario: A truck stop celebrates presidential shower-pressure policy with a broken demonstration; use the ordinary shower, fix the booth for pay, or leave.
Lead-in
A truck stop inspired by Trump’s showerhead order advertises executive water pressure. The demonstration has washed the suggestion box into the road.
Choices → responses
Take the ordinary shower → You get clean without declaring a constitutional victory.
Help repair the demonstration stand for pay → The plumbing accepts your wrench more readily than a proclamation.
Keep moving → You keep your resources and leave the opportunity behind.
The National Shower Demonstration
Scenario: A shower-pressure promotion needs someone to control its hose; take a paid maintenance shift, buy a normal wash, or leave.
Lead-in
A promotional booth for Trump’s showerhead order needs a volunteer to hold the hose. Its pressure is presidential; its fasteners are municipal.
Choices → responses
Take the paid maintenance shift → You earn twelve dollars restraining executive water pressure.
Buy a normal wash token → You wash off the road without becoming part of the demonstration.
Keep moving → You keep your resources and leave the opportunity behind.
Transit
The joke: ceremony and announcements are ready before anything people can ride. The hook is Chicago’s transit funding pause, not a claim that every project was canceled. Background
The Ribbon-Cutting Holding Pattern
Scenario: Transit advocates have ceremony supplies but paused funding; contribute supplies, take a paid survey shift, or leave.
Lead-in
A transit advocacy booth displays Chicago’s funding-pause news. The ribbon is ready, the scissors are ready, and neither is accepted as public transportation.
Choices → responses
Supply the volunteers’ outreach table → The campaign gets lunch. Commuters still need actual transit.
Take a paid rider-survey shift → You collect nine dollars and several unusually specific sighs.
Keep moving → You keep your resources and leave the opportunity behind.
Media and health
Rewrite the lead-ins, choices, and responses below. These are current English starters; preserve what each choice does. Before the arrow is the button; after it is the response.
Signal and access
The joke: encryption gets praised while nobody checks who has been invited. The hook is the administration’s Signal chat accidentally including a journalist. Background
Media Coach Onboarding
Scenario: A coach offers a quick media workshop after the Signal scandal; attend yourself or send your aides.
Lead-in
A friendly coach offers quick framing tips before the next checkpoint.
Choices → responses
Take the mini workshop → Your talking points get sharper for the next stand-up.
Send the aides instead → The aides feel prepared and the coach praises your prep.
Press Pool Q&A
Scenario: Reporters want more access to the bus; take live questions, screen them in advance, or send surrogates.
Lead-in
Traveling reporters request an extra rotation on the bus.
Choices → responses
Open the floor → You answer everything and set tomorrow's frame.
Limit to pre-submitted → The comms desk filters the pile effectively.
Hand off to surrogates → Your bench keeps the story tight while you rest.
Field Intel Courier
Scenario: Researchers bring files and surveys after a public chat-security scandal; use their findings, store them safely, or check for leaks.
Lead-in
Community researchers hand over drive images and surveys.
Choices → responses
Integrate their findings → New targets boost your oversight report.
Provide secure storage → They trust you with a critical archive.
Scan for leaks → You catch a rooted tablet before damage spreads.
Grassroots Signal Boost
Scenario: Organizers send encrypted updates; share them, verify them first, or forward everything unchecked.
Lead-in
Decentralized organizers beam encrypted updates from afar.
Choices → responses
Amplify across your channels → Cross-network sharing keeps pressure balanced.
Vet every packet → You catch a forged update before it spreads.
Forward raw feeds → Unverified blasts generate frantic callbacks.
National Security Family Plan
Scenario: A supposedly secure briefing chat contains relatives and service providers; audit the invite list, delegate, or request a formal review.
Lead-in
The encrypted checkpoint chat includes a cousin, a caterer, and your entire party. The encryption works. The invitation list needs diagnostics. The technicians await your decision.
Choices → responses
Audit the guest list → You remove the accidental guests. The encryption was never the problem.
Send staff instead → Your staff sort out the invitations while you miss the briefing.
Request a formal access review → The review consumes supplies but produces a documented access list.
Unscheduled Press Pool
Scenario: A dispatcher has mixed lunch orders and a sensitive briefing in one chat; separate the channels, rebuild contacts for pay, or leave.
Lead-in
After the administration’s Signal fiasco, a convoy dispatcher discovers the lunch-order chat also contains tomorrow’s security briefing. And a restaurant critic.
Choices → responses
Separate lunch from the sensitive channel → The critic is removed. The sandwiches remain under review.
Rebuild the contact list for a fee → Eight dollars buys more contact hygiene than the old system had.
Keep moving → You keep your resources and leave the opportunity behind.
Weather and spin
The joke: the forecast is edited to please authority; the weather declines to cooperate. The historical hook is Sharpiegate. Background
Impromptu Press Briefing
Scenario: Journalists want quotes before departure; answer openly, send a statement, or offer individual interviews.
Lead-in
Local journalists ask for quick quotes before the convoy moves on.
Choices → responses
Take every question → The coverage boosts the route's visibility.
Send a written statement → You save energy but the press notes the dodge.
Pull one-on-one interviews → Depth pieces win the cycle without sloppy headlines.
Media Ambush Drill
Scenario: A media coach uses Sharpiegate-style pressure to test your answers; practice yourself, train staff, or rest.
Lead-in
A crisis PR coach ambushes you with rapid-fire hypotheticals.
Choices → responses
Take every question → You refine answers before the cameras roll.
Workshop with staff → Your team internalizes the new message grid.
Postpone for sleep → You refuse to drill exhausted and stay sharp later.
Whistleblower Watch Party
Scenario: Whistleblowers testify late into the night about political interference with evidence; moderate, save clips, or let staff recap.
Lead-in
A secure bunker hosts remote testimonies late into the night.
Choices → responses
Moderate live → You cross-examine while the stream surges.
Clip highlights later → You queue the best testimony for release windows.
Let staff recap → You rest while trusted aides capture takeaways.
The Forecast Has Been Corrected
Scenario: A publicity desk has redrawn a bad forecast as sunshine; follow real shelter advice, trust the drawing, or leave.
Lead-in
Inspired by Sharpiegate, the local spin desk has drawn sunshine over the rain radar. The windshield refuses to cooperate.
Choices → responses
Use the forecaster’s actual shelter advice → You stay dry. The marker remains scientifically unnecessary.
Trust the freshly drawn sun → The briefing is cheerful. Your socks are a rebuttal.
Keep moving → You keep your resources and leave the opportunity behind.
Alternative Weather Desk
Scenario: A contractor wants favorable weather drawn onto an unfavorable forecast; publish the original, take money to alter it, or leave.
Lead-in
A briefing contractor has learned the wrong lesson from Sharpiegate: every unfavorable forecast needs a thicker pen. You are offered the corrections desk.
Choices → responses
Publish the meteorologist’s original chart → The weather is unchanged. The record is finally accurate.
Accept six dollars to redraw the sunshine → The chart improves politically. The clouds remain insubordinate.
Keep moving → You keep your resources and leave the opportunity behind.
Wellness and evidence
The joke: scientific confidence arrives before the supporting science. The hook is the MAHA report’s nonexistent studies and citation errors, later corrected by HHS. Background
Raw Milk Stand
Scenario: A wellness stall promotes raw milk with dubious research citations; drink it, decline, or buy sealed snacks.
Lead-in
The vendor’s health claims cite nine studies, three of which are expected to exist shortly. A medal-wearing cow lends institutional credibility.
Choices → responses
Drink the milk → You brave the calcium gamble.
Politely decline → You hype their safety checklist instead.
Buy shelf-stable snacks → The vendor upsells you sealed treats.
Town Hall Drift
Scenario: A town hall has drifted into health claims and disputed studies; redirect it, let people vent, or organize workgroups.
Lead-in
A classic-mode town hall needs calming words.
Choices → responses
Guide the conversation → You steer the agenda back to housing.
Let them vent → You ride out the venting with patient nods.
Break into workgroups → Facilitators scoop the loudest voices aside.
Clinic Triage
Scenario: Volunteer medics offer practical care amid inflated wellness claims; decline, accept fluids, or donate bandages.
Lead-in
A volunteer medic wagon offers hydration and quick checks.
Choices → responses
Wave them off → You insist the team keeps moving despite the concern.
Take a saline break → Medics insist on fluids and make you sit a spell.
Donate spare bandages → You bolster the triage cache and breathe easier.
Peer-Reviewed by the Cow
Scenario: A wellness vendor claims scientific authority from a cow and questionable citations; check the studies, buy sealed food, or leave.
Lead-in
A MAHA-inspired vendor assures you that every health claim has a citation. The bibliography is mostly the cow’s LinkedIn endorsements.
Choices → responses
Check whether the studies exist → Several citations retire to spend more time with their families.
Buy sealed snacks instead → Your lunch has an ingredients list and no honorary doctorate.
Keep moving → You keep your resources and leave the opportunity behind.
Citation Repair Is Hiring
Scenario: A newspaper needs help repairing MAHA-related citations; take the paid assignment, wave away the errors, or leave.
Lead-in
A local paper needs a freelancer after the MAHA report’s citation errors. The editor promises more real dollars than some references had real authors.
Choices → responses
Take the paid fact-checking assignment → Fifteen dollars. Several broken citations. One intact standard of evidence.
Declare the links spiritually valid → The editor declines your services. Confidence briefly replaces verification.
Keep moving → You keep your resources and leave the opportunity behind.
Bibliography Emergency Room
Scenario: A clinic treats missing research references as an emergency; check citations for pay, use ordinary care supplies, or leave.
Lead-in
After the MAHA report’s errors, a clinic has opened a citation triage desk. The references have impressive titles but no detectable authors.
Choices → responses
Take the paid reference-checking shift → Twelve dollars earned. The bibliography regains a pulse.
Use the clinic’s ordinary care supplies → Your crew improves under a treatment that exists.
Keep moving → You keep your resources and leave the opportunity behind.
Town conversations

Write one resident’s sharp, conversational reaction to the local situation. The scenario is the factual setup; the resident line below is the editable satire. Keep proposed cuts, warnings, and temporary interruptions distinct from events that happened.
Minneapolis
Scenario: The University of Minnesota reported dozens of terminated federal research awards and affected staff in 2025. Background
Resident’s line
